claim: Approximately 30% of embryonic stem cells (ESCs) die after exiting self-renewal.
source: Approximately, 30% of embryonic stem cells (ESCs) die after exiting self-renewal, but regulators of this process are not well known.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations to previous studies (Bashamboo et al., 2006; Duval et al., 2000) in the introduction.

claim: ESCs lacking Yap1 experience massive cell death upon the exit from self-renewal.
source: We first reveal that ESCs lacking Yap1 experience massive cell death upon the exit from self-renewal.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A-C demonstrating increased cell death in Yap1 KO cells during differentiation.

claim: Yap1 contextually protects differentiating, but not self-renewing, ESCs from hyperactivation of the apoptotic cascade.
source: We subsequently show that Yap1 contextually protects differentiating, but not self-renewing, ESC from hyperactivation of the apoptotic cascade.
evidence: This is demonstrated by data in Figure 1A showing minimal cell death in undifferentiated cells regardless of genotype, while differentiated Yap1 KO cells show dramatically higher death rates.

claim: Yap1 strongly activates anti-apoptotic genes via cis-regulatory elements.
source: Mechanistically, Yap1 strongly activates anti-apoptotic genes via cis-regulatory elements while mildly suppressing pro-apoptotic genes, which moderates the level of mitochondrial priming that occurs during differentiation.
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data (Figure 4) showing Yap1 occupancy on anti-apoptotic gene regulatory elements and dual luciferase assays demonstrating their activation.

claim: Yap1 mildly suppresses pro-apoptotic genes.
source: Mechanistically, Yap1 strongly activates anti-apoptotic genes via cis-regulatory elements while mildly suppressing pro-apoptotic genes, which moderates the level of mitochondrial priming that occurs during differentiation.
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data in Figure 3C showing increased expression of pro-apoptotic genes in Yap1 KO cells and dual luciferase assays in Figure 4E.

claim: Yap1 moderates the level of mitochondrial priming that occurs during differentiation.
source: Mechanistically, Yap1 strongly activates anti-apoptotic genes via cis-regulatory elements while mildly suppressing pro-apoptotic genes, which moderates the level of mitochondrial priming that occurs during differentiation.
evidence: This is demonstrated by JC-10 assays in Figure 5A showing increased loss of mitochondrial membrane potential in Yap1 KO cells during differentiation.

claim: Individually modulating the expression of single apoptosis-related genes targeted by Yap1 is sufficient to augment or hinder survival during differentiation.
source: Individually modulating the expression of single apoptosis-related genes targeted by Yap1 is sufficient to augment or hinder survival during differentiation.
evidence: This is demonstrated by experiments in Figure 6 showing that overexpression of Bcl-2 or Bcl-xL reduces cell death in Yap1 KO cells, while knockdown of these genes increases cell death in WT cells.

claim: When Hippo signaling is active, kinases Lats1/2 phosphorylate Yap1, leading to cytoplasmic sequestration.
source: When Hippo signaling is active, kinases Lats1/2 phosphorylate Yap1, leading to cytoplasmic sequestration (Hao et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Hao et al., 2008.

claim: When Hippo signaling is inactive, Yap1 translocates to the nucleus to co-activate or co-repress numerous target genes with interacting partner proteins such as Tead factors.
source: When Hippo signaling is inactive, Yap1 translocates to the nucleus to co-activate or co-repress numerous target genes with interacting partner proteins such as Tead factors (Kim et al., 2015; Stein et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Kim et al., 2015 and Stein et al., 2015.

claim: Nuclear translocation of Yap1 occurs shortly after withdrawal of leukemia inhibitory factor (LIF) in mouse embryonic stem cells.
source: Previous research indicated that, in mouse embryonic stem cells (ESCs), nuclear translocation of Yap1 occurs shortly after withdrawal of leukemia inhibitory factor (LIF), a cytokine that maintains self-renewal, and that depletion of Yap1 inhibits differentiation, whereas overexpression (OE) of Yap1 stimulates differentiation (Chung et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Chung et al., 2016.

claim: Depletion of Yap1 inhibits differentiation in mouse ESCs.
source: Previous research indicated that, in mouse embryonic stem cells (ESCs), nuclear translocation of Yap1 occurs shortly after withdrawal of leukemia inhibitory factor (LIF), a cytokine that maintains self-renewal, and that depletion of Yap1 inhibits differentiation, whereas overexpression (OE) of Yap1 stimulates differentiation (Chung et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Chung et al., 2016.

claim: Overexpression of Yap1 stimulates differentiation in mouse ESCs.
source: Previous research indicated that, in mouse embryonic stem cells (ESCs), nuclear translocation of Yap1 occurs shortly after withdrawal of leukemia inhibitory factor (LIF), a cytokine that maintains self-renewal, and that depletion of Yap1 inhibits differentiation, whereas overexpression (OE) of Yap1 stimulates differentiation (Chung et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Chung et al., 2016.

claim: Deletion of Yap1 leads to embryonic lethality by E10.5.
source: Deletion of Yap1 leads to embryonic lethality by E10.5 although the downstream mechanism remains poorly characterized (Morin-Kensicki et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Morin-Kensicki et al., 2006.

claim: Withdrawal of LIF causes the death of 30% or more of ESCs.
source: A previous study has reported that withdrawal of LIF causes the death of 30% or more of ESCs (Bashamboo et al., 2006; Duval et al., 2000), and around 30% of human ESCs are also annexin V positive when they exit from self-renewal (Dravid et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Bashamboo et al., 2006 and Duval et al., 2000.

claim: Around 30% of human ESCs are annexin V positive when they exit from self-renewal.
source: A previous study has reported that withdrawal of LIF causes the death of 30% or more of ESCs (Bashamboo et al., 2006; Duval et al., 2000), and around 30% of human ESCs are also annexin V positive when they exit from self-renewal (Dravid et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Dravid et al., 2005.

claim: A proposed function of apoptosis during ESC differentiation is to cull cells that fail to exit self-renewal, thus promoting efficient differentiation.
source: A proposed function of apoptosis during ESC differentiation is to cull cells that fail to exit self-renewal, thus promoting efficient differentiation (Wang et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Wang et al., 2015.

claim: Apoptosis eliminates defective cells during human neural progenitor differentiation.
source: This process is not limited to ESCs, as defective cells are executed during human neural progenitor differentiation as well (Jaeger et al., 2015), and apoptosis eliminates self-reactive and non-reactive lymphocytes during T and B cell differentiation (Francelin, 2011; Nemazee, 2017; Opferman, 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Jaeger et al., 2015.

claim: Apoptosis eliminates self-reactive and non-reactive lymphocytes during T and B cell differentiation.
source: This process is not limited to ESCs, as defective cells are executed during human neural progenitor differentiation as well (Jaeger et al., 2015), and apoptosis eliminates self-reactive and non-reactive lymphocytes during T and B cell differentiation (Francelin, 2011; Nemazee, 2017; Opferman, 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Francelin, 2011; Nemazee, 2017; and Opferman, 2008.

claim: Cell death was dramatically higher (up to >70%) in Yap1 KO cells 72 hr after LIF withdrawal.
source: While ~30% cell death was observed from wild-type (WT) cells as previously reported (Bashamboo et al., 2006), cell death was dramatically higher (up to >70%) in Yap1 KO cells 72 hr after LIF withdrawal (Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by LDH assay data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Cell death in both WT and Yap1 KO ESCs was substantially reduced after supplementation with Z-VAD-FMK, a pan-caspase inhibitor.
source: In both cases, cell death was substantially reduced after supplementation with Z-VAD-FMK (zVAD), a pan-caspase inhibitor, but not with necrostatin-1, which blocks necroptosis.
evidence: This is demonstrated by LDH assay data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Cell death in both WT and Yap1 KO ESCs was not reduced by necrostatin-1, which blocks necroptosis.
source: In both cases, cell death was substantially reduced after supplementation with Z-VAD-FMK (zVAD), a pan-caspase inhibitor, but not with necrostatin-1, which blocks necroptosis.
evidence: This is demonstrated by LDH assay data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Undifferentiated ESCs had extremely low rates of cell death regardless of genotype.
source: Undifferentiated cells had extremely low rates of cell death regardless of genotype (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by LDH assay data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Additional Yap1 KO clones in J1, CJ7, and E14 ESC lines experienced drastically heightened cell death during differentiation, but not self-renewal.
source: An additional J1 Yap1 KO clone as well as Yap1 KO clones established in the CJ7 and E14 ESC lines (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C) also experienced drastically heightened cell death during differentiation, but not self-renewal (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by LDH assay data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Depletion of Yap1 using shRNA-mediated knockdown dose-dependently increased cell death during differentiation.
source: Furthermore, depletion of Yap1 using shRNA-mediated knockdown (KD) dose-dependently increased cell death during differentiation (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D and E).
evidence: This is demonstrated by RT-qPCR and LDH assay data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D and E.

claim: Stable Yap1 overexpression reduced cell death to approximately 10% during differentiation.
source: Finally, measuring cell death in stable Yap1 OE cell lines (Figure 1-figure supplement F) reduced cell death to a mere ~10% during differentiation (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by LDH assay data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Ablation of Yap1 specifically exacerbates apoptosis during ESC differentiation.
source: Thus, Yap1 is key for survival during ESC differentiation, and ablation of Yap1 specifically exacerbates apoptosis.
evidence: This is inferred from the combined data showing increased cell death in Yap1 KO cells that is rescued by caspase inhibitors.

claim: Both the relative proportion of Casp3 positive cells and the fluorescent intensity of the Casp3 substrate fluorescent probe were higher in Yap1 KO differentiating ESCs.
source: Both the relative proportion of Casp3 positive cells and the fluorescent intensity of the Casp3 substrate fluorescent probe were higher in Yap1 KO differentiating ESCs (dESCs), and this was correlated with an increased proportion of annexin V positive cells (Figure 1E and F).
evidence: This is demonstrated by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1E and F.

claim: Increased Casp3 activation in Yap1 KO dESCs was correlated with an increased proportion of annexin V positive cells.
source: Both the relative proportion of Casp3 positive cells and the fluorescent intensity of the Casp3 substrate fluorescent probe were higher in Yap1 KO differentiating ESCs (dESCs), and this was correlated with an increased proportion of annexin V positive cells (Figure 1E and F).
evidence: This is demonstrated by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1E and F.

claim: Immunoblot analysis confirmed faster and more intense cleavage of Casp9, Casp3, and Parp1 in Yap1 KO cells during differentiation.
source: Immunoblot analysis confirmed faster and more intense cleavage of Casp9, Casp3, and Parp1 in Yap1 KO cells during differentiation (Figure 1G).
evidence: This is demonstrated by immunoblot data shown in Figure 1G.

claim: Treatment with staurosporine induced faster and more drastic activation of Casp3 and Parp1 in Yap1 KO than in WT dESCs.
source: This treatment induced faster and more drastic activation of Casp3 and Parp1 in Yap1 KO than in WT dESCs as quickly as two hours after addition, reflecting a vastly heightened sensitivity to apoptosis-inducing stress (Figure 1—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: This is demonstrated by immunoblot data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1G.

claim: By 60 hr after LIF removal, all caspases tested were approximately two-fold more active in Yap1 KO cells than in WT.
source: By 60 hr after LIF removal, all caspases tested were approximately two-fold more active in Yap1 KO cells than in WT (Figure 1H).
evidence: This is demonstrated by luminescent caspase activity assay data shown in Figure 1H.

claim: Knockdown of Casp9 reduced cell death during differentiation, particularly in Yap1 KO cells where cell death was reduced to WT levels.
source: As expected, KD of Casp9 reduced cell death during differentiation, and this was particularly stark for Yap1 KO cells, where cell death was reduced to WT levels without Casp9 KD (Figure 1I).
evidence: This is demonstrated by LDH assay data shown in Figure 1I.

claim: The abnormally high rates of apoptosis in Yap1 KO cells are sustained by heightened Casp9 activation.
source: This implied that the abnormally high rates of apoptosis in Yap1 KO cells are sustained by heightened Casp9 activation.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Casp9 knockdown rescues cell death in Yap1 KO cells to WT levels.

claim: mRNA expression of caspases was relatively equal between Yap1 KO cells and WT cells during differentiation.
source: We observed that mRNA expression of caspases was relatively equal between Yap1 KO cells and WT cells during differentiation (Figure 1—figure supplement 1I).
evidence: This is demonstrated by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1I.

claim: Protein levels of Casp3 showed similar fluctuations in dESCs for both WT and KO cells.
source: Additionally, protein levels of Casp3 showed similar fluctuations in dESCs for both WT and KO cells; although Casp8 and Casp9 were elevated in Yap1 KO cells (Figure 1G).
evidence: This is demonstrated by immunoblot data shown in Figure 1G.

claim: Casp8 and Casp9 protein levels were elevated in Yap1 KO cells during differentiation.
source: Additionally, protein levels of Casp3 showed similar fluctuations in dESCs for both WT and KO cells; although Casp8 and Casp9 were elevated in Yap1 KO cells (Figure 1G).
evidence: This is demonstrated by immunoblot data shown in Figure 1G.

claim: dESCs without Yap1 experienced much higher rates of cell death compared to WT cells in N2B27 medium (neural ectoderm fate), which could be rescued by zVAD.
source: Utilizing N2B27 medium (neural ectoderm fate) or low serum DMEM supplemented with IDE1 (definitive endoderm fate) (Borowiak et al., 2009), we again observed that dESCs without Yap1 experienced much higher rates of cell death compared to WT cells, which could be rescued by zVAD (Figure 2B and C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by LDH assay data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: dESCs without Yap1 experienced much higher rates of cell death compared to WT cells in low serum DMEM supplemented with IDE1 (definitive endoderm fate), which could be rescued by zVAD.
source: Utilizing N2B27 medium (neural ectoderm fate) or low serum DMEM supplemented with IDE1 (definitive endoderm fate) (Borowiak et al., 2009), we again observed that dESCs without Yap1 experienced much higher rates of cell death compared to WT cells, which could be rescued by zVAD (Figure 2B and C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by LDH assay data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: EpiLCs lacking Yap1 underwent substantially higher cell death than WT by day 3, and zVAD reduced cell death in both genotypes to low, basal rates.
source: As expected, EpiLCs lacking Yap1 underwent substantially higher cell death than WT by d3, and zVAD reduced cell death in both genotypes to the low, basal rates experienced in 2i media (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by LDH assay data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Treatment with as low as 1 μM verteporfin before the exit from self-renewal phenocopied Yap1 KO.
source: While treatment with as low as 1 μM verteporfin before the exit from self-renewal phenocopied Yap1 KO, treatment during late differentiation had more modest effects on cell death, and treated cells had death rates nearly identical to untreated by d7 (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is demonstrated by LDH assay data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Treatment with verteporfin during late differentiation had more modest effects on cell death, and treated cells had death rates nearly identical to untreated by day 7.
source: While treatment with as low as 1 μM verteporfin before the exit from self-renewal phenocopied Yap1 KO, treatment during late differentiation had more modest effects on cell death, and treated cells had death rates nearly identical to untreated by d7 (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is demonstrated by LDH assay data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Loss of Yap1 increases rates of apoptosis in ESCs directly after the exit from self-renewal, regardless of the ultimate lineage those ESCs are destined for.
source: Together, these data suggest that loss of Yap1 increases rates of apoptosis in ESCs directly after the exit from self-renewal, regardless of the ultimate lineage those ESCs are destined for.
evidence: This is inferred from data showing increased cell death in Yap1 KO cells across multiple differentiation conditions (neural, endoderm, EpiLC).

claim: After 72 hr of LIF withdrawal, a deficiency in three key anti-apoptotic proteins (Bcl-2, Bcl-xL, and Mcl-1) was detected in Yap1 KO cells by immunoblot.
source: After 72 hr of LIF withdrawal, we detected a deficiency in three key anti-apoptotic proteins (Bcl-2, Bcl-xL, and Mcl-1) in Yap1 KO cells by immunoblot (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by immunoblot data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Immunocytochemistry confirmed reduced expression of Bcl-2 and Mcl-1 in Yap1 KO dESCs compared to WT.
source: Immunocytochemistry confirmed reduced expression of Bcl-2 and Mcl-1 in Yap1 KO dESCs compared to WT, as well as lower mitochondrial content as measured by MitoTracker dye (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and B)
evidence: This is demonstrated by immunocytochemistry data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and B.

claim: Yap1 KO dESCs had lower mitochondrial content as measured by MitoTracker dye compared to WT.
source: Immunocytochemistry confirmed reduced expression of Bcl-2 and Mcl-1 in Yap1 KO dESCs compared to WT, as well as lower mitochondrial content as measured by MitoTracker dye (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and B)
evidence: This is demonstrated by immunocytochemistry data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and B.

claim: Bcl-2 and Mcl-1 strongly colocalized with the mitochondria (weighted colocalization coefficient ~ 0.7–0.9).
source: as expected, Bcl-2 and Mcl-1 strongly colocalized with the mitochondria (weighted colocalization coefficient for all samples ~ 0.7–0.9).
evidence: This is demonstrated by colocalization analysis of immunocytochemistry data.

claim: In WT ESCs, Bcl2 was strongly upregulated in all differentiation conditions tested.
source: In WT ESCs, we found that Bcl2 was strongly upregulated in all differentiation conditions tested; pro-apoptotic genes such as Puma (Bbc3) and Noxa (Pmaip1) were also activated, whereas Bcl2l1 and Mcl1 either stayed constant or were weakly upregulated (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Pro-apoptotic genes such as Puma (Bbc3) and Noxa (Pmaip1) were activated during differentiation in WT ESCs.
source: In WT ESCs, we found that Bcl2 was strongly upregulated in all differentiation conditions tested; pro-apoptotic genes such as Puma (Bbc3) and Noxa (Pmaip1) were also activated, whereas Bcl2l1 and Mcl1 either stayed constant or were weakly upregulated (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Bcl2l1 and Mcl1 either stayed constant or were weakly upregulated during differentiation in WT ESCs.
source: In WT ESCs, we found that Bcl2 was strongly upregulated in all differentiation conditions tested; pro-apoptotic genes such as Puma (Bbc3) and Noxa (Pmaip1) were also activated, whereas Bcl2l1 and Mcl1 either stayed constant or were weakly upregulated (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Comparing Yap1 KO cells to WT ESCs by day 2, there was a general trend for decreased anti-apoptotic gene expression (most consistently Bcl2) and increased pro-apoptotic gene expression.
source: Comparing Yap1 KO cells to WT ESCs, by d2, we found a general trend for decreased anti-apoptotic gene expression (most consistently Bcl2) and increased pro-apoptotic gene expression (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The defect in anti-apoptotic gene expression in Yap1 KO cells worsened over time in -LIF.
source: This defect worsened over time in -LIF (Figure 3D) and was particularly stark for Bcl2, which was upregulated as much as 80 to 100-fold by 96 hr in WT ESCs upon differentiation (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is demonstrated by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Bcl2 was upregulated as much as 80 to 100-fold by 96 hr in WT ESCs upon differentiation.
source: This defect worsened over time in -LIF (Figure 3D) and was particularly stark for Bcl2, which was upregulated as much as 80 to 100-fold by 96 hr in WT ESCs upon differentiation (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is demonstrated by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Transient overexpression of Yap1 after differentiation resulted in modest induction of Bcl2, Bcl2l1, and Mcl1, as well as modest repression of Bbc3 and Bmf.
source: To reinforce this observation, we examined the expression of apoptosis-related genes after 2d of transient OE of Yap1 after 3d of differentiation total, and found a modest induction in Bcl2, Bcl2l1, and Mcl1, as well as a modest repression of Bbc3 and Bmf (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Differentiation induces the expression of a group of anti-apoptotic genes in WT cells, but this induction is debilitated after Yap1 KD.
source: Using RNA-seq data from a previous study (Chung et al., 2016), we found that differentiation induces the expression of a group of anti-apoptotic genes in WT cells, but this induction is debilitated after Yap1 KD (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by analysis of RNA-seq data from Chung et al., 2016, shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Yap1 may function as a master regulator in proper maintenance or induction of anti-apoptotic genes (particularly Bcl2) during differentiation.
source: Collectively, these data show that Yap1 may function as a master regulator in proper maintenance or induction of anti-apoptotic genes (particularly Bcl2) during differentiation, and it may also dampen the upregulation of pro-apoptotic genes.
evidence: This is inferred from the combined data showing Yap1's effects on anti-apoptotic and pro-apoptotic gene expression.

claim: Yap1 may dampen the upregulation of pro-apoptotic genes during differentiation.
source: Collectively, these data show that Yap1 may function as a master regulator in proper maintenance or induction of anti-apoptotic genes (particularly Bcl2) during differentiation, and it may also dampen the upregulation of pro-apoptotic genes.
evidence: This is inferred from the combined data showing Yap1's effects on anti-apoptotic and pro-apoptotic gene expression.

claim: ChIP-seq of Yap1 detected 8453 peaks significantly enriched over the BirA control during differentiation and only 699 peaks in +LIF.
source: We performed ChIP-seq of Yap1 using ESCs overexpressing FLAG-Bio-Yap1 (FB-Yap1) under differentiation (-LIF, 72 hr) and self-renewal (+LIF) conditions, detecting 8453 peaks significantly enriched over the BirA control above threshold between duplicates during differentiation and only 699 peaks in +LIF, reflecting its known cytoplasmic localization during self-renewal.
evidence: This is demonstrated by ChIP-seq data generated in this study.

claim: Many of the differentiation-related Yap1 ChIP-seq peaks were intergenic as well as in promoters.
source: Many of the differentiation-related peaks were intergenic as well as in promoters (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by gene feature analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Yap1 occupancy was positively correlated with degree of gene downregulation upon Yap1 KD.
source: Yap1 occupancy was positively correlated with degree of gene downregulation upon Yap1 KD, although some upregulated genes upon KD were associated with unusually low Yap1 occupancy (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by integrated analysis of ChIP-seq and RNA-seq data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Some genes upregulated upon Yap1 KD were associated with unusually low Yap1 occupancy.
source: Yap1 occupancy was positively correlated with degree of gene downregulation upon Yap1 KD, although some upregulated genes upon KD were associated with unusually low Yap1 occupancy (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by integrated analysis of ChIP-seq and RNA-seq data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Yap1 peaks were strongly correlated with increased Ep300 (p300) occupancy during differentiation.
source: By integrating data from a previous study investigating enhancer patterns at different stages of pluripotency (Buecker et al., 2014), we found that Yap1 peaks were strongly correlated with increased Ep300 (p300) occupancy during differentiation (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by integrated analysis of ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: A physical interaction between Yap1 and p300 was confirmed during ESC differentiation using co-immunoprecipitation.
source: We confirmed a physical interaction between Yap1 and p300 as well as one of its known cofactors, Tead4 (Chen et al., 2010), during ESC differentiation using co-immunoprecipitation (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B), consistent with known Yap1 nuclear localization in dESCs (Chung et al., 2016).
evidence: This is demonstrated by co-IP data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: A physical interaction between Yap1 and Tead4 was confirmed during ESC differentiation using co-immunoprecipitation.
source: We confirmed a physical interaction between Yap1 and p300 as well as one of its known cofactors, Tead4 (Chen et al., 2010), during ESC differentiation using co-immunoprecipitation (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B), consistent with known Yap1 nuclear localization in dESCs (Chung et al., 2016).
evidence: This is demonstrated by co-IP data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Motif analysis revealed a significant enrichment of the Tead factor motif in addition to Zic3 and AP-1 complex (JunB and Fra1 (Fosl1)) motifs in the center of Yap1 peaks.
source: Indeed, motif analysis revealed a significant enrichment of the Tead factor motif in addition to Zic3 and AP-1 complex (JunB and Fra1 (Fosl1)) motifs in the center of Yap1 peaks, whereas Esrrb (a negative control) was not found (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C and D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by motif analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C and D.

claim: An increase in H3K27ac, an activating histone mark, was confirmed in Yap1 peaks during differentiation.
source: Finally, since p300 possesses histone acetyltransferase activity, we confirmed an increase in H3K27ac, an activating histone mark, in Yap1 peaks during differentiation (Figure 4—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is demonstrated by ChIP-seq analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1E.

claim: Gene ontology analysis of genes bound by Yap1 and downregulated by Yap1 KD mainly yielded terms related to cell migration and motility, and regulation of cell death was also statistically significant.
source: Gene ontology (GO) analysis of genes bound by Yap1 and downregulated by Yap1 KD mainly yielded terms related to cell migration and motility, and regulation of cell death was also statistically significant (Figure 4—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is demonstrated by GO analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1F.

claim: In Yap1 KO cells, luciferase constructs with regulatory elements associated with Mcl1, Bcl2, or Bcl2l1 have lower luciferase activity relative to WT cells.
source: In Yap1 KO cells, luciferase constructs with regulatory elements associated with Mcl1, Bcl2, or Bcl2l1 have lower luciferase activity relative to WT cells, while regulatory elements associated with Bmf, Pmaip1, and Bbc3 led to higher luciferase activity (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by dual luciferase assay data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: In Yap1 KO cells, regulatory elements associated with Bmf, Pmaip1, and Bbc3 led to higher luciferase activity relative to WT cells.
source: In Yap1 KO cells, luciferase constructs with regulatory elements associated with Mcl1, Bcl2, or Bcl2l1 have lower luciferase activity relative to WT cells, while regulatory elements associated with Bmf, Pmaip1, and Bbc3 led to higher luciferase activity (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by dual luciferase assay data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Transient OE of Yap1 led to higher luciferase activity with anti-apoptotic gene regulatory elements and lower luciferase activity with pro-apoptotic gene regulatory elements.
source: Meanwhile, transient OE of Yap1 led to higher luciferase activity with anti-apoptotic gene regulatory elements and lower luciferase activity with pro-apoptotic gene regulatory elements (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is demonstrated by dual luciferase assay data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Transient OE of Yap1 in Yap1 KO cells rescued enhancer function to levels comparable to Yap1 OE in WT cells for Mcl1 distal and Bcl2 intronic tandem enhancers.
source: Transient OE of Yap1 in Yap1 KO cells rescued enhancer function to levels comparable to Yap1 OE in WT cells, whereas OE of Yap1 S79A, a mutant less capable of binding to Tead factors (Schlegelmilch et al., 2011), only mildly rescued Mcl1's enhancer's activity and failed to rescue Bcl2's enhancer's activity at all (Figure 4F).
evidence: This is demonstrated by dual luciferase assay data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: OE of Yap1 S79A, a mutant less capable of binding to Tead factors, only mildly rescued Mcl1's enhancer's activity and failed to rescue Bcl2's enhancer's activity.
source: Transient OE of Yap1 in Yap1 KO cells rescued enhancer function to levels comparable to Yap1 OE in WT cells, whereas OE of Yap1 S79A, a mutant less capable of binding to Tead factors (Schlegelmilch et al., 2011), only mildly rescued Mcl1's enhancer's activity and failed to rescue Bcl2's enhancer's activity at all (Figure 4F).
evidence: This is demonstrated by dual luciferase assay data shown in Figure 4F and supported by citation to Schlegelmilch et al., 2011.

claim: Ablation of the Tead binding sequence from the Mcl1 enhancer not only eliminated its Yap1 responsiveness, but also nearly abolished its enhancer activity.
source: Furthermore, ablation of the Tead binding sequence (ΔTBS) from the Mcl1 enhancer not only eliminated its Yap1 responsiveness, but also nearly abolished its enhancer activity (Figure 4G).
evidence: This is demonstrated by dual luciferase assay data shown in Figure 4G.

claim: Yap1 occupancy on apoptosis-related genes seems to be relatively conserved (r =~0.5) among different human cancer cell types.
source: Intriguingly, Yap1 occupancy on apoptosis-related genes seems to be relatively conserved (r =~0.5) among different human cancer cell types (Figure 4—figure supplement 1I and J).
evidence: This is demonstrated by correlation analysis of YAP1 ChIP-seq data from different human cell types shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1I and J.

claim: Yap1 peaks in mouse dESCs correlated with Tead1 and Tead4 peaks in other mouse cell types.
source: Additionally, Yap1 peaks in mouse dESCs also correlated with Tead1 and Tead4 peaks in other mouse cell types, and signal tracks show similar occupancy patterns particularly for Bcl2 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1K and L).
evidence: This is demonstrated by correlation analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1K and L.

claim: Mitochondria were equally primed during self-renewal in WT and Yap1 KO ESCs.
source: Whereas mitochondria were equally primed during self-renewal, all four differentiation conditions (-LIF, neural, endoderm, EpiLC) resulted in a greater loss of mitochondrial membrane potential (Δψ) in Yap1 KO cells normalized to WT ESCs (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by JC-10 assay data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: All four differentiation conditions (-LIF, neural, endoderm, EpiLC) resulted in a greater loss of mitochondrial membrane potential (Δψ) in Yap1 KO cells normalized to WT ESCs.
source: Whereas mitochondria were equally primed during self-renewal, all four differentiation conditions (-LIF, neural, endoderm, EpiLC) resulted in a greater loss of mitochondrial membrane potential (Δψ) in Yap1 KO cells normalized to WT ESCs (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by JC-10 assay data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Inhibition of anti-apoptotic proteins increased Δψ in dESCs more than in self-renewing ESCs.
source: As expected, inhibition of anti-apoptotic proteins increased Δψ in dESCs more than in self-renewing ESCs (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by JC-10 assay data with BH3 mimetics shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Deletion of Yap1 significantly sensitized dESCs, but not undifferentiated ESCs, to Δψ loss post BH3 mimetic treatment.
source: Furthermore, deletion of Yap1 significantly sensitized dESCs, but not undifferentiated ESCs, to Δψ loss post BH3 mimetic treatment.
evidence: This is demonstrated by JC-10 assay data with BH3 mimetics shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Mere inhibition of anti-apoptotic proteins was sufficient to cause cell death, particularly in dESCs, even before apoptosis normally occurs during differentiation.
source: Our results showed that mere inhibition of anti-apoptotic proteins was sufficient to cause cell death, particularly in dESCs, even before apoptosis normally occurs during differentiation (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by LDH assay data with BH3 mimetics shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Loss of Yap1 significantly amplified cell death in response to BH3 mimetics at almost all concentrations tested, but only during differentiation.
source: Strikingly, loss of Yap1 significantly amplified cell death in response to BH3 mimetics at almost all concentrations tested, but only during differentiation (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by LDH assay data with BH3 mimetics shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Ablation of Yap1 enhanced addiction to Mcl-1 and Bcl-xL; inhibition of either protein resulted in 2-3x greater cell death in Yap1 KO than WT.
source: Ablation of Yap1 also enhanced addiction to Mcl-1 and Bcl-xL; inhibition of either protein resulted in 2-3x greater cell death in Yap1 KO than WT (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by LDH assay data with BH3 mimetics shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Loss of Yap1 leads to increased mitochondrial priming during differentiation, which subsequently sensitizes Yap1 KO to excessive activation of the apoptotic cascade.
source: Thus, loss of Yap1 leads to increased mitochondrial priming during differentiation, which subsequently sensitizes Yap1 KO to excessive activation of the apoptotic cascade.
evidence: This is inferred from the combined data showing increased mitochondrial membrane potential loss and heightened sensitivity to BH3 mimetics in Yap1 KO cells.

claim: Knockdown of Bmf or Puma mildly reduced cell death in Yap1 KO cells during differentiation but not in WT ESCs.
source: Therefore, we performed KD of Bmf and Puma (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A and B) and this mildly reduced cell death in Yap1 KO cells during differentiation but not in WT ESCs (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by LDH assay data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Inducible OE of Bmf or Puma accelerated apoptosis during differentiation, particularly in Yap1 KO cells.
source: Inducible OE of either factor (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C and D) accelerated apoptosis during differentiation, particularly in Yap1 KO cells, and Puma promoted cell death more strongly than Bmf (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is demonstrated by LDH assay data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: Puma promoted cell death more strongly than Bmf during differentiation.
source: Inducible OE of either factor (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C and D) accelerated apoptosis during differentiation, particularly in Yap1 KO cells, and Puma promoted cell death more strongly than Bmf (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is demonstrated by LDH assay data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: Puma promiscuously binds to all known anti-apoptotic Bcl-2 family proteins, whereas Bmf binds only weakly to Mcl-1, preferring Bcl-2, Bcl-xL, and Bcl-w.
source: This difference may be because Puma promiscuously binds to all known anti-apoptotic Bcl-2 family proteins, whereas Bmf binds only weakly to Mcl-1, preferring Bcl-2, Bcl-xL, and Bcl-w (Chen et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Chen et al., 2005.

claim: Yap1's pro-survival function is primarily via activation of anti-apoptotic proteins.
source: Thus, although Yap1's pro-survival function is primarily via activation of anti-apoptotic proteins, heightened expression of individual pro-apoptotic BH3-only proteins seems to contribute to enhanced cell death during differentiation of Yap1 KO cells.
evidence: This is inferred from the combined data showing strong effects of anti-apoptotic protein modulation and modest effects of pro-apoptotic protein modulation.

claim: Heightened expression of individual pro-apoptotic BH3-only proteins contributes to enhanced cell death during differentiation of Yap1 KO cells.
source: Thus, although Yap1's pro-survival function is primarily via activation of anti-apoptotic proteins, heightened expression of individual pro-apoptotic BH3-only proteins seems to contribute to enhanced cell death during differentiation of Yap1 KO cells.
evidence: This is demonstrated by experiments showing that knockdown or overexpression of Bmf or Puma affects cell death rates.

claim: Mcl-1 expression was already reduced in Yap1 KO cells 28 hr after LIF withdrawal compared to WT ESCs.
source: Mcl-1 expression was already reduced in Yap1 KO cells 28 hr after LIF withdrawal compared to WT ESCs. Yap1 KO cells were acutely sensitive to inhibition (4 hr) of either Mcl-1 or Bcl-2/Bcl-xL/Bcl-w, indicating increased mitochondrial priming even at such an early timepoint (Figure 5F).
evidence: This is demonstrated by immunoblot data shown in Figure 5F.

claim: Yap1 KO cells were acutely sensitive to inhibition (4 hr) of either Mcl-1 or Bcl-2/Bcl-xL/Bcl-w at 28 hr after LIF withdrawal, indicating increased mitochondrial priming even at such an early timepoint.
source: Mcl-1 expression was already reduced in Yap1 KO cells 28 hr after LIF withdrawal compared to WT ESCs. Yap1 KO cells were acutely sensitive to inhibition (4 hr) of either Mcl-1 or Bcl-2/Bcl-xL/Bcl-w, indicating increased mitochondrial priming even at such an early timepoint (Figure 5F).
evidence: This is demonstrated by immunoblot data shown in Figure 5F.

claim: Deficiency in Mcl-1 expression helps explain heightened apoptotic activation in Yap1 KO cells even before differences in Bcl-2 expression become apparent.
source: Since Mcl-1 is much more highly expressed than both Bcl-2 and Bcl-xL, we surmise that deficiency in its expression helps explain heightened apoptotic activation in Yap1 KO cells even before differences in Bcl-2 expression become apparent (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Mcl-1 is reduced early in differentiation while Bcl-2 differences appear later.

claim: Stable overexpression of Bcl-xL in Yap1 KO cells reduced cell death to levels comparable to WT.
source: We stably overexpressed Yap1 (as a positive control to complement the KO) and Bcl-xL (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A) and inducibly overexpressed Bcl-2 (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B, C and D) in Yap1 KO cells, which reduced cell death in Yap1 KO to levels comparable to WT (Figure 6A and B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by LDH assay data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Inducible overexpression of Bcl-2 in Yap1 KO cells reduced cell death to levels comparable to WT.
source: We stably overexpressed Yap1 (as a positive control to complement the KO) and Bcl-xL (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A) and inducibly overexpressed Bcl-2 (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B, C and D) in Yap1 KO cells, which reduced cell death in Yap1 KO to levels comparable to WT (Figure 6A and B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by LDH assay data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Inducible OE of Taz reduced cell death in both Yap1 KO cells and WT cells to levels just below uninduced WT cells, perhaps via upregulation of Bcl-xL.
source: Intriguingly, inducible OE of Taz, a Yap1 paralog also possessing a Tead-binding domain, reduced cell death in both Yap1 KO cells and WT cells to levels just below uninduced WT cells, perhaps via upregulation of Bcl-xL (Figure 6C and D), and Figure 6—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is demonstrated by LDH assay and immunoblot data shown in Figure 6C, D, and Figure 6—figure supplement 1F.

claim: Knockdown of Bcl-xL, Mcl-1, or Bcl-2 in WT ESCs individually increased cell death during differentiation 1.5 to 2-fold compared to controls.
source: Conversely, KD of Bcl-xL, Mcl-1 (Figure 6—figure supplement 1F), or Bcl-2 (Figure 6—figure supplement 1G) in WT ESCs individually increased cell death during differentiation 1.5 to 2-fold compared to controls (Figure 6E and F, Figure 6—figure supplement 1H).
evidence: This is demonstrated by LDH assay data shown in Figure 6E, F, and Figure 6—figure supplement 1H.

claim: OE of Bcl-2 led to increased induction of trophectoderm (Cdx2 and Gata3) and mesoderm markers (Gsc and T).
source: Surprisingly, we found that OE of Bcl-2 led to increased induction of trophectoderm (Cdx2 and Gata3) and mesoderm markers (Gsc and T), while KD of Bcl-2 tended to reduce induction of lineage markers.
evidence: This is demonstrated by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 6G.

claim: KD of Bcl-2 tended to reduce induction of lineage markers.
source: Surprisingly, we found that OE of Bcl-2 led to increased induction of trophectoderm (Cdx2 and Gata3) and mesoderm markers (Gsc and T), while KD of Bcl-2 tended to reduce induction of lineage markers.
evidence: This is demonstrated by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 6G.

claim: KD of Bcl-xL or Mcl-1 had no effect on lineage marker induction.
source: However, KD of Bcl-xL or Mcl-1 had no effect on lineage marker induction (Figure 6G and Figure 6—figure supplement 1I and J).
evidence: This is demonstrated by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 6G and Figure 6—figure supplement 1I and J.

claim: Anti-apoptotic factors transcriptionally regulated by Yap1 are critical for dESC survival.
source: Taken together, these data clearly demonstrate that anti-apoptotic factors transcriptionally regulated by Yap1 are critical for dESC survival, and that OE or KD of each apoptotic factor can significantly shift the balance between survival and death.
evidence: This is inferred from the combined data showing that modulation of anti-apoptotic factors affects cell death rates during differentiation.

claim: OE or KD of each apoptotic factor can significantly shift the balance between survival and death during ESC differentiation.
source: Taken together, these data clearly demonstrate that anti-apoptotic factors transcriptionally regulated by Yap1 are critical for dESC survival, and that OE or KD of each apoptotic factor can significantly shift the balance between survival and death.
evidence: This is demonstrated by experiments showing that modulation of individual apoptotic factors affects cell death rates.

claim: Bcl-2 has previously unknown roles in regulation of ESC lineage specification.
source: The results additionally suggest the previously unknown roles of Bcl-2 in regulation of ESC lineage specification, as only its roles in self-renewal have been deeply probed (Yamane et al., 2005).
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Bcl-2 modulation affects lineage marker expression, which has not been previously reported.

claim: Activation of Casp3 during ESC differentiation was extremely heterogeneous, with many cells changing their morphology without detectable caspase activation.
source: Intriguingly, our Casp3 live imaging assay revealed that activation of Casp3 was extremely heterogeneous, with many cells changing their morphology during differentiation without detectable caspase activation.
evidence: This is demonstrated by live imaging data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: OE of Bcl-2 improved induction of essential trophectoderm and mesoderm markers.
source: One unexpected finding from our study is that OE of Bcl-2 improved induction of essential trophectoderm and mesoderm markers, and KD of Bcl-2 (but not Mcl-1 or Bcl-xL) conversely hampered such induction.
evidence: This is demonstrated by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 6G.

claim: KD of Bcl-2 (but not Mcl-1 or Bcl-xL) hampered induction of trophectoderm and mesoderm markers.
source: One unexpected finding from our study is that OE of Bcl-2 improved induction of essential trophectoderm and mesoderm markers, and KD of Bcl-2 (but not Mcl-1 or Bcl-xL) conversely hampered such induction.
evidence: This is demonstrated by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 6G and Figure 6—figure supplement 1I and J.

claim: Yap1 binding peaks on apoptosis-related genes are conserved across several human cancer cell types.
source: Additionally, we noted that Yap1 binding peaks on apoptosis-related genes are conserved across several human cancer cell types, which corroborates previous findings (Rosenbluh et al., 2012).
evidence: This is demonstrated by correlation analysis of YAP1 ChIP-seq data from different human cell types and supported by citation to Rosenbluh et al., 2012.

claim: Addiction to anti-apoptotic factors is a defining characteristic of cancer cells.
source: Since addiction to anti-apoptotic factors is a defining characteristic of cancer cells, the regulation mechanisms we have elucidated may be broadly applicable to how Yap1 promotes tumorigenesis.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about cancer cell biology.

claim: Yap1 robustly promotes survival of ESCs during differentiation by direct transcriptional regulation of apoptotic genes.
source: In sum, our study has clearly demonstrated that Yap1 robustly promotes survival of ESCs during differentiation by direct transcriptional regulation of apoptotic genes.
evidence: This is the main conclusion drawn from all the experimental data presented in the study.
